newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees 4.5 pct monthly yr/yr GDP rise - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees 4.5 pct monthly yr/yr GDP rise - report.

text.p: Peru's Central Reserve Bank is forecasting an average monthly year-on-year Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 4.5 percent for the rest of 1996.

In an interview in Monday's edition of the daily Gestion, the bank's general manager, Javier de la Rocha, said this growth would be guaranteed by mining and petroleum investments, increased availability of anchovies for fishing, higher industrial production and recovery in the construction sector.
According to latest official figures, year-on-year GDP growth was 5.1 percent in July, compared with 7.4 percent year-on-year growth in the same month last year.
The economy grew 2.0 percent between January and July, compared with 8.7 percent in the same period of 1995.
The government is now predicting annual growth of between three and four percent in 1996, down from initial projections of five to six percent due to an economic slowdown earlier in the year.
